scope: Read-only source audit against the prior mainnet host census and the qualified v5 caller-profile-2 large-caller slice. No new full-block replay, proof, disk benchmark or peak-memory measurement.
result: No deterministic full-block cap or field-validation blocker found from the available census. Actual execution lookup demands, retained fetch metadata and proof allocations remain admitted during collection/proving.

census.scope: Previously collected host-only census; not a new v5 proof admission. Segmentation does not change the full execution's event/address census.

memory_and_range.partition_note: A full shard holds 23 or 24 full-height instances depending on the actual 21/22-per-row requests. The exact counts and ordered partition are recomputed from real traces; 23+23+23+16 is only the conservative 22-per-event packing.
memory_and_range.word_geometry_note: log22 is below the packed replay's maximum admitted log24. Only one sorted trace/PCS is live; roots/claims and small range counters survive.

source_and_program_caps.source_file_formula: first_touch_keys * (9-byte touch + 16-byte endpoint) + (initial_nonzero_rw_words + public_input_touches) * 8; deliberately overcounts register endpoints and overlapping input/RW image words
source_and_program_caps.program_fetch_count_note: Approximately total cycles plus terminal fetch; 139,214,857 is below M31 modulus 2,147,483,647. Per-address multiplicities cannot exceed the total.

qualified_keccak_slice.scope: Fresh large caller proof slice already qualified; does not independently admit the full ordinary native segment or later caller roster.

lookup_demands.note: The observed large Keccak slice does not approach 500M. Later native/SHA/signer/clock demand must still pass exact collection admission; a group cannot split an oversized individual execution.

metadata_and_transport.base_store_file_count_formula: 4 * executions + 5 * caller_executions + lookup_groups + 85 memory + 4 range + 1 ROM
metadata_and_transport.caller_retention: Only a value-owned Proposal survives each segment; witnesses, PCS and local counter sets are released.
metadata_and_transport.rom_retention: Planning.Record retains complete/caller Fetch arrays through Assembly. They are sorted positive multiplicities per distinct fetched program address, not one record per instruction. This is explicitly bounded metadata, not fully streamed program metadata.
metadata_and_transport.retention_conclusion: No actual aggregate fetch count was available to prove a 256MiB cap failure. The cap is checked cumulatively before each retained array is copied; it remains a genuine first-pass admission gate.

disk_bounds.available_space_observation: Parent checked df at 11:37 before the v2 launch; this is available space at that observation, not reserved capacity.
disk_bounds.sort_peak_formula: 3 * event_count * 17: retained raw + current sorted runs + replacement merge output. Old merge inputs are deleted after each merged group is written.
disk_bounds.recursive_file_formula: (67 leaves + at most 66 parents + 1 outer) * 128MiB; conservative parent count
disk_bounds.pessimistic_total_note: Rounded upward: raw+final event files + full 16GiB counter-source allowance + full 64GiB base Store allowance + recursive file bound + 512MiB each source/policy + manifest and one publication-temporary allowance. Actual 67-group counter files are only about 0.744GiB. Temporary sorting and proof production happen in separate phases.
disk_bounds.conclusion: No concrete disk-space blocker against the reported 177GiB available. Store's 64GiB cap excludes event spool, counter source and recursive proof files, so it is not a whole-output-directory cap.

runtime_limitations: This audit establishes no sufficiency guarantee for runtime RSS, active proof allocation peaks, the largest later ordinary/caller geometry, actual lookup demand or the retained ROM fetch roster. Real collection/proof/transport admission remains mandatory.
